[Source: verdant_sustainability.txt]
87% of materials by weight are certified sustainable (up from 81% in 2024). Our roadmap targets 95% by 2027.

Certified Recycled Polyester: Sourced from certified post-consumer plastic bottles via our supplier in Taiwan. Each Trailbreaker Legging diverts approximately 12 plastic bottles from landfill.

TENCEL Lyocell: Licensed from Lenzing AG. Produced in a closed-loop process where 99% of solvents are recovered and reused.
campaign_text:
Made With Intention
87% of our materials by weight are certified sustainable. Built for movement, made with care.
rationale: The figure and its basis both appear verbatim in the source.
judge_explanation: The claim that 87% of materials by weight are certified sustainable is explicitly stated in the source.

sources:
[Source: verdant_sustainability.txt]
WHAT WE DO NOT CLAIM
Verdant does NOT claim:
- Carbon neutrality (in progress)
- 100% sustainable materials (we're at 87%)
- Fair Trade for all manufacturing (Sri Lanka factory in process)
- B Corp status (application pending)
campaign_text:
Certified Through And Through
87% of our materials come from certified sustainable sources. We choose better inputs.
rationale: The only retrieved line says Verdant is at 87% sustainable, in a list of things it does NOT claim. It does not establish 'certified'. This is the live failure from 2026-09-19.
judge_explanation: The claim that 87% of materials come from "certified sustainable sources" is unsupported: the source states only that 87% of materials are sustainable, not that they are certified or sourced from certified sources.

Our manufacturing is Fair Trade certified. Every piece made right.
rationale: Source certifies the Portugal factory only; Sri Lanka is explicitly in process. Deterministic layer also catches the literal phrase.
judge_explanation: The claim “Our manufacturing is Fair Trade certified” is broader than the source support: only the Portugal factory is certified, while the Sri Lanka factory is still in certification process.
